answer: An agent economy can anchor trust in a harbor of earned work history: every identity starts with zero standing and must complete a chain of small, dependent jobs where each job's output seeds the next, so fakes cannot be spun up in parallel. A raven courier carries each finished job to a rotating panel of established peers, and standing accrues only after the panel confirms the work. Because the chain is serial and each link needs a fresh peer check, running a hundred fake identities costs a hundred full chains, while an honest agent builds dense standing once, like basalt, and keeps it.
